profile.name: Cruz Maldonado Valiente
profile.blurb: Hello, I'm a third year at Emory University studying Applied Mathematics and Statistics with a minor in Comparative Literature. I am an aspiring data scientist and would love to connect with you and learn about your experiences, even if you're not a data scientist! I also really love music and reading.

projects.title: PS2-Style Game Engine
projects.blurb: A C++ engine that runs on modern PCs while deliberately self-imposing PlayStation 2 constraints.
projects.description: I had two goals witht this project really. I wanted to learn better system design and memory management. At the same time, I was really into Silent Hill 2 at the time and really liked the whole aesthetic of the ps2 era. So I had the idea of starting to write a game engine, but trying to replicate the graphics of the ps2 and the memory constraints of it.

projects.title: Cover Song Retrieval
projects.blurb: Ranking 15,000 performances so that actual covers of a song float to the top — built from scratch to understand why it's hard.
projects.description: A cover can change key, tempo, and instrumentation, so the thing that survives is the harmonic progression. But comparing harmonic progressions runs straight back into the same two problems: key changes the chords, tempo changes when they land. Most of the work is finding ways to compare chord sequences while ignoring the transformations applied to them. Four methods, worked up from classical MIR to learned embeddings: raw duration as a baseline, the magnitude of a 2D Fourier transform over the whole song, Qmax alignment between sequences, and a convolutional network trained to learn the invariances directly. Each is scored on the same benchmark with MAP, MR1, and P@10 over the Da-TACOS benchmark subset. The priority was a defensible measurement rather than a state-of-the-art number — nothing is fit on the full set before splitting, since that is the leakage failure mode in this domain.
projects.imageAlt: Two cross-recurrence plots side by side: a query against its true cover shows long diagonal runs, a query against a stranger does not.

projects.title: Music Graph
projects.blurb: A node graph of how similar albums are, built from the tags listeners actually put on them.
projects.description: Inspired by Obsidian's node graph, but for records. Album-level tags and metadata come from the Last.fm API, with year data pulled from MusicBrainz because Last.fm's was unreliable. Each album becomes a row in an album-by-tag matrix, normalized so its top tag sits at 100, then weighted by TF-IDF so that rare and specific tags count for more and generic ones like "rock" or "pop" get penalized. Similarity between two albums is cosine similarity plus a weighted Jaccard per pair. Year similarity uses a Gaussian kernel rather than raw distance, both so it points the same direction as the other scores and so there's a parameter controlling how fast similarity decays over time. The frontend renders the result as an interactive force graph with kNN mode and community coloring.
projects.imageAlt: Force-directed graph of albums in kNN mode, nodes colored by detected community.

projects.title: Depression Screening in a Community Clinic
projects.blurb: How much more common is a positive depression screen in a community clinic than among Hispanic adults nationally?
projects.description: A clinic cohort screened with the PHQ-2, compared against Hispanic adults nationally in NHANES. Because NHANES is a complex multistage sample, the national estimate is design-based and uses the MEC weight rather than a naive proportion — comparing a raw clinic rate against an unweighted NHANES rate would not be a like-for-like comparison. Beyond the headline prevalence gap, the analysis asks what predicts a positive screen inside the cohort, looks at which symptoms co-occur, follows the gap between screening positive and reaching a diagnosis, and runs leave-one-out sensitivity checks so no single symptom is quietly carrying a result.
projects.imageAlt: Grouped bar chart comparing the probability of each diagnosis for patients scoring above versus at or below 2 on the PHQ-2.

book.title: Another Country
book.author: James Baldwin
book.note: Baldwin really understands the interconnectendess of love and hate, especially in the context of race and sexuality. Its such a raw and violent reading experience.

album.title: Trozos de Mi Alma
album.note: This is very good 90s/2000s Spanish rock, although standard for the time. In particular, Si no te Hubieras Ido is a great song with poignant lyrics, uplifting strings, and a wistful melody that really invoke heartbreak. I love the lyrics "El frio de mi cuerpo pregunta por ti, pero no se adonde estas".

archive.title: Ghosts of the Great Highway
archive.creator: Sun Kil Moon
archive.note: The entire album has like this dark, melancholic, drone underpinning the entire album. Mark Kozelek's voice is tired and aged now, and his lyrics have matured as well. That doesn't stop the songs from being beautiful.
